defects: Conclusion structure differs: GOLD compares Module.rank S N vs Module.rank R N for the SAME module N under two compatible module structures (S-module restricted to R via IsScalarTower), whereas PRODUCED compares Module.rank R M (original module) vs Module.rank (FractionRing R) (M ⊗[R] FractionRing R) (an extension-of-scalars/base-change module) — these are different propositions; deriving one from the other requires an extra unstated fact (that rank_R M equals rank_R of its base-changed module M⊗S).

PRODUCED restricts to R an integral domain with S hardcoded as FractionRing R, while GOLD is stated for a general CommRing R with S an arbitrary type satisfying IsFractionRing R S via localization at a submonoid p ≤ R⁰ (nonzero divisors) — GOLD is strictly more general (covers non-domain R / total fraction rings and abstract fraction-ring types), a generality PRODUCED drops.

GOLD carries an essential auxiliary structure — a separate module M, a localization map f : M →ₗ[R] N, [IsLocalizedModule p f], and submonoid p ≤ R⁰ relating N to a localization of M — none of which has any counterpart in PRODUCED; PRODUCED's variable named M plays an entirely different role (it is the module being base-changed, not an auxiliary pre-localization module).
PRODUCED only requires M : AddCommMonoid (module over a ring), whereas GOLD requires N : AddCommGroup — a mismatched additive structure hypothesis between the two formalizations.

PRODUCED's conclusion introduces the specific tensor-product construction M ⊗[R] FractionRing R for the localized module, while GOLD leaves N abstract (any S-module satisfying the scalar tower/localization hypotheses) — not a mere notational variant but a different way of presenting the localized object.
